body.heading: A dance floor in the dark
paragraphs: Inside a dark hive, a bee who has found good flowers performs a dance on the honeycomb. Her sisters gather round and feel her movements.
The dance is shaped like a figure of eight, with a wiggly run down the middle. It is called the waggle dance.

body.heading: What the dance says
paragraphs: The wiggly run points the way. Its direction, compared to the sun, tells the other bees which way to fly.
The longer the wiggly run lasts, the further away the flowers are. The dance is a map, drawn with a body instead of a pencil.

body.heading: Try being a bee
paragraphs: Stand in a room and do a short wiggly walk to mean near, and a long wiggly walk to mean far. Can your family guess your message?
Bees have been reading these dances for millions of years. It is one of the cleverest languages in the animal world.

takeaway: Honey bees give directions by dancing — the waggle dance points to the flowers and tells how far they are.
safetyNotes: This is an indoor activity about bees — never approach a real hive or disturb bees outdoors.
screenFreeExtension: Invent your own dance directions to lead a family member to a hidden teddy.
